items.headline: OpenAI introduces GPT-6 Cyber, a restricted model for vetted security defenders
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Cyber behind its application-only 'Daybreak Red' access tier, aimed at authorized vulnerability research and exploit development. The company rates it 'Critical' under its Preparedness Framework, up from 'High' for its predecessor, reflecting a sharp jump in offensive-security capability that also raises dual-use risk.

items.headline: DOJ charges three men in $129 million AI deepfake CEO and lawyer fraud scheme
items.summary: Federal prosecutors in New York charged three defendants with using AI-generated voice and video to impersonate executives and attorneys, tricking companies into wiring over $129 million. The case is one of the largest publicly documented uses of generative AI for financial fraud to date.

items.headline: Perplexity launches 'Teammates,' always-on AI agents for Max subscribers
items.summary: Perplexity rolled out persistent AI agents that take on ongoing roles within a workspace, pulling in prior projects, skills, and memory, and integrating with Slack. The move escalates competition with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Microsoft in the race to sell autonomous 'AI coworker' products.

items.headline: Researchers unveil WorldParticle, a single AI model that simulates many physical materials
items.summary: A team from MIT CSAIL, UBC, Meta, and several other universities built one transformer that can simulate cloth, fluids, elastic solids, and granular materials within a unified particle-based framework, potentially replacing a patchwork of specialized physics simulators used in graphics, robotics, and engineering.

items.headline: NVIDIA Research debuts AgentBaton to cut costs of long-running AI agents
items.summary: NVIDIA Research, with HKUST and UIUC, released AgentBaton, a lightweight detector that mid-task hands off long-horizon agentic work from a capable, expensive model to a cheaper one, reporting large API cost savings on agent benchmarks without major accuracy loss.

items.headline: Ai2 releases ToyBlocks, an open robot-simulation framework for training manipulation policies
items.summary: The Allen Institute for AI launched ToyBlocks, the first 'FoundationWorld,' an open-source tabletop simulator paired with pre-trained vision-language-action models and tens of thousands of demonstrations, aimed at making robot-learning research more reproducible and accessible.

items.headline: Apple opens Siri AI to all developers in new Developer Preview
items.summary: Apple shipped a developer preview letting any app connect its custom actions to Siri AI, a step toward a more agentic assistant, though App Store apps won't be able to ship the integration until spring 2027. It follows reports of internal pressure to accelerate Apple's AI roadmap.

items.headline: Chai Discovery partners with Roche to apply AI drug design across its pipeline
items.summary: Biotech AI startup Chai Discovery announced a collaboration with Roche to use its AI models for drug discovery programs, extending a string of 2026 pharma partnerships that also include GSK and Eli Lilly, as AI-designed molecule pipelines move further into mainstream pharma R&D.

items.headline: MoleculeMind's AI platform narrows GPCR drug candidates from billions to dozens
items.summary: A Shanghai-based AI drug-discovery effort reported using generative molecular modeling to computationally screen candidate compounds against notoriously hard-to-target GPCR proteins, shrinking a search space of billions down to a handful for lab testing, though independent validation of therapeutic activity is still pending.

items.headline: OpenAI's deadline to cut off Cursor's model access arrives after SpaceX acquisition
items.summary: OpenAI's self-imposed November 12 deadline to stop supplying AI models to the coding tool Cursor took effect, following SpaceX's acquisition of Cursor's parent company and a dispute over whether that change of control violates OpenAI's terms of service. Cursor retains access to Grok, Claude, and Gemini models.
